assumptions: 'Success rate' means attempt-level success rate: successful attempts divided by all attempts, with each retry counted as a separate attempt. Order-level and technical rates are shown alongside.

The period 17 Sep 2026 is compared with the immediately preceding period of equal length (16 Sep 2026); the detected anomaly window and baseline used for the statistical comparison were 17-18 Sep versus 10-16 Sep.
Failure codes are reported per 100 attempts.
caveats: The comparison covers a two-day dip window (17-18 Sep) against the preceding week (10-16 Sep), so the overall figures include 18 Sep as well as 17 Sep.
The hourly timeline provided covers 16 Sep only, so the exact start and end time of the incident is not established from this evidence.
Hourly drops in the overnight hours were not statistically significant because attempt counts are small.

facts.text: Attempt success rate over the dip window (17-18 Sep) fell 3.10pp, from 90.07% (83,268 attempts, 10-16 Sep) to 86.98% (22,790 attempts). The change is statistically significant and the confidence intervals do not overlap.
The daily rate was steady at roughly 89.2% to 90.4% through 3-14 Sep, and the anomaly detector flagged 17-18 Sep as a drop.

The segment scan ranked acquirer as the dimension that most concentrates the drop. Kestrel Bank's success rate fell 11.54pp, from 90.03% to 78.49%, while Northstar Bank (-0.44pp), Meridian Bank (+0.27pp) and Saffron Bank (+0.24pp) showed no significant change.

Within Kestrel Bank, only card payments were hit: debit card fell 30.11pp (86.42% to 56.31%), credit card fell 28.71pp (88.64% to 59.94%) and card EMI fell 23.87pp (80.67% to 56.80%). UPI, netbanking and wallet at Kestrel showed no significant change.

For Kestrel Bank card attempts, the acquirer timeout failure code (ACQ_TIMEOUT) rose from 0.26 to 32.27 failures per 100 attempts (803 failures in the dip window vs 22 in the baseline). Other failure codes were flat or lower.
Across all traffic, ACQ_TIMEOUT rose from 0.08 to 3.58 per 100 attempts (815 failures vs 69 in the baseline), and it was the only failure code with a large increase.
The data-quality scan found no issues in the data (0 findings).
The hour-of-day view shows significant drops in hours 11-15 and 17-23. The worst hour was hour 2, down 7.26pp, but that drop was not statistically significant (few attempts at night).

response.headline: The 17 Sep dip was driven by a card-payment problem at one acquirer, Kestrel Bank. Success rate over the 17-18 Sep dip window fell 3.10pp, from 90.07% to 86.98%, almost entirely because Kestrel Bank card attempts began timing out.

hypotheses.how_to_verify: Ask Kestrel Bank for their incident log and status for 17-18 Sep. Check hourly Kestrel card ACQ_TIMEOUT counts to find the start and end of the incident.
hypotheses.rationale: The drop is confined to one acquirer and to its three card methods, while Kestrel's UPI, netbanking and wallet and all other acquirers are unaffected. The failure code that surged is a technical acquirer timeout, not issuer declines or customer drop-off.
hypotheses.text: A technical issue on Kestrel Bank's card-processing path (for example an outage, degraded connectivity or capacity problem) caused card attempts to time out.

hypotheses.how_to_verify: Review the hourly Kestrel card timeline for 17-18 Sep to pinpoint when timeouts started and whether they have cleared.
hypotheses.rationale: Hourly success rates show significant drops from hour 11 onward, but the hourly timeline provided only covers 16 Sep, so the start time is not confirmed.
hypotheses.text: The incident began around the middle of 17 Sep and persisted into 18 Sep, rather than being a one-off spike.

recommendations.linked_fact_or_hypothesis: A technical issue on Kestrel Bank's card-processing path caused card attempts to time out.
recommendations.rationale: Kestrel card success rates fell by 24 to 30pp with timeouts at 32.27 per 100 attempts, so the fix sits with the acquirer.
recommendations.text: Escalate to Kestrel Bank to confirm and resolve the card timeout issue, and ask for a root-cause report.

recommendations.linked_fact_or_hypothesis: Within Kestrel Bank, only card payments were hit: debit card, credit card and card EMI.
recommendations.rationale: Other acquirers (Northstar, Meridian, Saffron) were stable, so shifting card volume could recover the lost successes.
recommendations.text: Consider temporarily routing card traffic away from Kestrel Bank to other acquirers while timeouts persist, if routing allows.

recommendations.linked_fact_or_hypothesis: For Kestrel Bank card attempts, ACQ_TIMEOUT rose from 0.26 to 32.27 failures per 100 attempts.
recommendations.rationale: ACQ_TIMEOUT moved from near zero to a very large share of attempts, a signal that is easy to threshold.
recommendations.text: Set up an alert on acquirer-level timeout rate per 100 attempts, by payment method, so a similar spike is flagged within the hour.
